name: Tryout
why: Borrowing a shop member's On Recruit is a neat twist on the shop, but it reads more like Green copying than Red recruiting.

name: Gather
why: Plain red income with a small recruit bonus; it's the color's anchor space, so its quiet sting is fine.

name: Walk-In
why: A free member off the top of the pile is exciting, and the +1 red to each rival softens it; few words.

name: Promote
why: Trading up with a rival is the heart of Red; the victim gets a member back so it stings fairly, and it works as catch-up.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote; taking a cheaper member is weaker and is mostly a way to dump a card or feed Foster Parents.

name: Initiation
why: A free 8-cost recruit in round III is a big burst a trailing player can grab.

name: Body Snatchers
why: A same-cost swap each round is clear and aimable, but often a sideways trade that feels small.

name: Volunteer
why: Cheap filler that only exists to trigger recruit cards and pad Red's member count; it does nothing when it fires.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two members for one buy fits Red's quantity idea, and the name matches what it does.

name: Proselytizers
why: A simple follower per recruit that grows with Red's free recruits; solid but quiet.

name: Mob
why: Pays the player who already leads in red members, round after round; rivals can race it, but it rewards the leader.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red each round for 5 resources is forgettable and rarely worth the buy.

name: Recruiter
why: Red income from recruiting stacks with free recruits; fine but small.

name: Patriarch
why: Game End per-member scoring is plain and rewards wide cults; nothing new for Red.

name: Foster Parents
why: Rewards Promote, Demote, Poach and swaps with +2 each time; ties Red's moving members to followers in very few words.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Worth 4 for 3 resources is close to a must-buy, and the ability is a small sting on top.

name: Panel
why: Promote or demote on recruit fits Red, but a cold reader has to look up what promote and demote do here.

name: Loyalists
why: A clean block against Red's swaps; it's unclear whether steals like Poach count as swaps.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple for going last is a real timing trade, but the Goes Last token takes a rules read.

name: Hold Up
why: A skip the victim can see coming and shrug off, and it can backfire on you; one clear sentence.

name: Right Away
why: Two turns in a row is clean; the small payout makes it mostly a way to set up Courier.

name: Last Call
why: A strong payoff for holding minions back, but the token plus 'other minions' is hard to follow on the table.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row is a big swing on the snake in few words, and it's a burst anyone can use to catch up.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in round III feels powerful and is open to whoever is behind.

name: Courier
why: Pays on double turns from the snake, Right Away and Crunch Time; ties Purple's timing to every color.

name: Night Watch
why: Watching for rivals taking the token is niche, and 'per minion on it' needs a careful read.

name: Night Owls
why: A free minion every later round is strong and clear but expensive and autopilot.

name: Early Birds
why: A cheap, clean counter to Hold Up and Bouncers that counts as 2.

name: Bouncers
why: Recruit-timed double skip is a table moment you can aim, combos with Gossip, and is cheap.

name: Bell Ringer
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do; unreadable condition
why: Nobody can tell when this fires; it needs a history of skips and token placement nobody can track.

name: Gossip
why: Feeds off every skip at the table, a passive trigger on something that happens often.

name: Timekeeper
why: Per-purple-member scoring copies Snobs and Old Money and has nothing to do with Purple's timing.

name: Closer
why: Racing for the last minion fits Purple's idea and plays off the Goes Last token and the contest.

name: Hot Streak
why: A big payout for chained turns, but counting 'turns in a row just before this one' is fiddly.

name: Picket Line
why: Cheap, worth 3, with a passive trickle from rivals on purple; quiet but a fair buy.

name: Toast
why: Big silver for you with a gift to everyone is the giving idea in one line.

name: Polish
why: A plain converter that does Yellow's job; useful but flat.

name: Party Gifts
why: Choosing who gets your silver gifts, with the silver contest at stake, is a real and social decision.

name: Potluck
hardFail: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn
why: Each rival picks what to hand over during your turn, and they always give their least useful resource.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver plus a convert repeats Polish; nothing new for Silver.

name: Largesse
why: A round III giveaway with a clear payoff and kingmaking tension; overlaps Party Gifts.

name: Godparent
why: Giving away a member for its cost in followers is a clean gift; it combos with Martyrs and Foster Parents.

name: Hostesses
why: A steady gift-for-followers each round; a rival notices the free silver.

name: Caterer
why: Pays on every gift, but it's unclear whether Toast's rival silver counts as gifted.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Dumping a cheap member for +4 every round is strong and aimable; it combos with cheap filler and Old Maid.

name: Toastmaster
why: +1 follower on your own spaces is forgettable.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources than you
why: Only pays when a rival holds more silver than you.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling your silver once is a big, well-timed contest swing with a small gift attached.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as any color is powerful but is the old Gold idea, not giving.

name: Charity Ball
why: A gift each time a rival recruits is passive and friendly; quiet value.

name: Creditor
why: A forced followers-for-silver trade aimed at the leader; a fair but mild sting.

name: Debt Collectors
why: A once-per-game silver grab that punishes hoarders; small.

name: High Society
why: Pays off rivals on Silver; same shape as Picket Line and quiet.

name: Harvest
why: Yellow's anchor: plain resources in colors you pick.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads the board for rivals' minions, but the name doesn't match and the payout is small.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards a new color of member, which pushes the variety idea; the bonus is conditional.

name: Housewarming
why: A free new-color recruit is a strong, clear variety play.

name: Melting Pot
why: Grows with the colors in your cult; a clean variety payoff.

name: Makeover
why: Rearranging every resource in round III can flip contests and complete full sets at the last moment.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills holes in your colors each round and helps a poor cult; 'have none of' needs a moment's read.

name: Duty Collector
why: A passive trickle when rivals recruit your colors; quiet.

name: Tourist
why: Followers for color variety each round; the same shape as Dyer and Caravan.

name: Seamstress
why: 'Double your full sets' doesn't say what doubles: the count for the contest, or the resources.

name: Dyer
why: Same as Tourist but pays yellow; it repeats its siblings.

name: Meddler
why: Messing up rivals' sets is a fair sting that fits Yellow, but who picks the new color is unclear.

name: Drifters
why: Cheap and flexible: counts toward any color's cards, like Mob, Snobs and Big Tent. The table needs a marker for the chosen color.

name: Big Tent
why: Rewards one member of many colors, so every recruit becomes a real choice.

name: Caravan
why: Big per-round income for variety, but it rewards a cult that's already broad.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
why: A clean full-set helper that matters only to the Yellow contest.

name: Savings
why: Blue income plus a shop dig before you recruit; the optional step is easy to forget.

name: Out of Style
why: Wiping one color from the shop blocks rivals in plain sight and pays per card sent away.

name: Peek
why: Stacking the pile and picking from it is a strong shop play, but wordy.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two buys in one turn is clear and strong.

name: Bury
why: Denying a shop member pays a little; the half-cost math adds words.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in round III is a burst any trailing player can use.

name: Hawker
hardFail: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn
why: Each rival decides in turn whether to buy during your turn, with many moving parts.

name: Patroness
why: Pays off every bury at the table, a passive trigger on Blue's main action.

name: Snobs
why: Per-color-member scoring; the same shape as Timekeeper and Old Money.

name: Window Shopper
why: Digging the shop for resources each round fits Blue but takes two steps to read.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn is a huge engine in four words, but at 9 it's hard to Promote or Demote away.

name: Scavenger
hardFail: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn
why: Asks its owner to decide and pay on a rival's turn.

name: Window Dressers
why: Cheap, worth 3, with a shop refresh; combos with Patroness.

name: Doormen
why: Swapping a rival's member out for a shop member is a fair, aimable sting, but wordy.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue per follower buy is forgettable.

name: Trendsetters
why: Cheap and worth 3, but the bury repeats Window Dressers.

name: Critic
why: +1 follower when a rival buys blue is too small to notice.

name: Help Yourself
why: Aimable theft that grows each round; the check on hoards, with fair counterplay.

name: Stash
why: Plain fuel, the same as Gather and Allowance; Magenta's anchor.

name: Lie Low
why: A small steal plus a shield; a clean defensive choice.

name: Heist
why: Stealing followers directly is a big, aimable swing at the leader.

name: Shake Down
hardFail: turn flow: asks a player to choose during another player's turn; victim chooses their own punishment
why: The victim picks their own punishment on your turn, and that feels bad.

name: Poach
why: Taking any rival's member in round III is a big swing, and late enough to be fair.

name: Cutpurse
why: A small steal each round that always hits the richest; clear catch-up, but small.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap way into Magenta: steal 3 when you recruit it.

name: Grifter
why: The steal grows with your cult size, so it rewards whoever is already ahead.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A theft right before contests are scored can swing a contest, and everyone sees it coming.

name: Desperado
why: Built-in catch-up that powers up every Magenta steal for the player in last.

name: Extortionist
why: A bigger Cutpurse; it repeats its sibling.

name: Bodyguards
why: A clean block against all theft; once it's out, theft has no answer to it.

name: Double Agent
why: A swap that plants itself in a rival's cult; reads more like Red, and the rival gets an empty card.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a member every round from the same rival before round III, and that rival has little answer.

name: Shoplifter
why: A steal on every recruit; it stacks quietly.

name: Fence
why: Turns being robbed into magenta; the victim shrugs and the thief thinks twice.

name: Allowance
why: Plain fuel, the same as Stash and Gather; White's anchor.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for a big recruit is a nice spend reward, but the round-by-round rate needs a read.

name: Exchange
why: Resources into followers at 2 for 1, a small, plain conversion.

name: Farewell
why: Casting out a member for its cost in followers combos with Martyrs; clear and punchy.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell paid in white instead; it repeats its sibling.

name: Cash In
why: A round III cash-out that rewards having saved white; one clear line.

name: Recluse
why: Pays for a small cult, a real catch-up angle and a reason to stay lean.

name: Barker
why: An extra follower buy on every member buy is strong, but the word 'recruit followers' takes a read.

name: Heiresses
why: A once-per-game white bump; forgettable.

name: Brokers
why: Cheap, worth 3, and adds to every White space that pays followers.

name: Misers
why: Saving white for the end versus spending it is a real hold-or-spend call.

name: Raiders
why: Stealing followers is Magenta's job.

name: Cashier
why: Does what Cash In already does.

name: Money Changers
why: Pays off everyone's follower buys; cheap and steady.

name: Martyrs
why: Leaving pays its cost, so Farewell, Godparent and thieves all feed it; few words that play off the whole board.

name: Old Money
why: Per-white-member scoring copies Snobs and Timekeeper and works against White's own idea.

name: Magpie
why: Turning everything into white sets up Cash In and Misers; it's a timing call.

name: Build Up
why: Green's plain anchor space.

name: Echo
why: Copying the previous action plays off whatever just happened; four words and endless depth.

name: Reprise
why: Doubling your own best action is clear; it's quieter than Echo.

name: Sample
why: Borrowing a rival's On Recruit reads the table and fits copying.

name: Cover
why: Copying an empty space lets you use a spot without blocking it; a clean twist.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Replaying all your On Recruits is a big round III payoff for the cult you built.

name: Song Request
why: An extra copy each round of a rival's space; strong and it reads the table.

name: Impersonator
why: Wearing a rival's ability is fun, but the table has to remember what it is copying.

name: Impressionist
why: A small passive on every copy at the table; quiet.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubling copied gains is a strong Green engine, but pricey.

name: Fan Club
why: Copying the leader's space is catch-up with a clear target.

name: Roadie
why: Copy income that grows with green members; modest.

name: Stunt Double
why: Copying the action you just took when it joins is clear but one-off and small.

name: Tribute Band
why: Doing a rival's whole round of actions is a huge moment, but at 14 it's hard to answer.

name: Doppelganger
why: Copying your best member is strong; the table has to remember which member it copied.

name: Agents
why: A cheap block against Green copying.

name: Encore
why: Doubling your next On Recruit is a fun, well-timed copy; it needs a marker until used.

name: Party Crasher
why: Breaking the one-minion-per-space rule once is a fair surprise that undoes a block.

name: Alchemists
why: Cheap and worth 3, and it removes color limits for recruiting; overlaps Smooth Talkers.

name: Extra Hand
why: One extra minion for 9 is a poor deal and the same in any cult.

name: Line Cutters
why: Worth 3 for 2 and it turns off the fewest-followers-first catch-up; a must-buy for the leader.

name: Old Maid
why: A curse to pass on with Promote, Godparent or Doormen. Nobody buys it, and the player who gets it loses 5 followers with no answer.

name: Dabblers
why: Counting as 2 members of any color helps the member-count contests; 'wild' needs explaining.

name: Cheerleaders
why: Pays only the player already winning contests.

name: Victors
hardFail: single-member card with a plural name
why: Rewards contest winners with more of the color they won.

name: Anarchist
why: Swapping any two members each round is a strong table lever; the cost-within-2 rule needs a check.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancelling a contest you can't win is clear catch-up, and everyone can plan around it.

name: Con Men
why: A big steal on a colorless card does Magenta's job.

name: Sore Loser
why: Punishes the contest leader for whoever won none; clear catch-up the leader can see coming.
